body:
I gave some review on this function name [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90510#discussion_r1755763934) in the predecessor PR:

> Another naming nitpick: "function extension" is an unclear term that we don't really use anywhere else.
> 
> Maybe `load_extension_from_function()`?
> 
> Or, if we can decide on an overall name for this feature we could use that term. So, if we standardize on "LibGodot", then this could be `load_libgodot_extension()`? Or, if we standardize on "embedded", then it could be `load_embedded_extension()`?

body:
I like `"libgodot://"` better than the `"res://__LibGodot"` that I commented on [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/90510#discussion_r1755772483) on the predecessor PR.

However, we should make sure that everyone is OK with using this invalid path prefix!

Yeah, this is a bit of a weird one. For reference, the point of this is to create something "extension-like" that is simply based on a callback, rather than loading an entire dynamic library (which we can't do because, in this environment, Godot *is* the library.) This feature is a bit overbuilt for the purposes of libgodot but I figured I'd leave it in because other people seem to want it.

I'd personally lean towards "load_extension_from_function()", but I'm not wedded to any of the terminology here and will happily change on request.
